g.text: Is the Gap Real, or Just Noise?
Control and treatment each produce a distribution of outcomes across users --
the platform's only job is deciding whether their means actually differ, or just look different by chance.
individual outcomes vary far more than the two means do,
which is exactly why this needs a statistical test, not a glance.
The gap is unlikely to be chance --
reject the null, treat the effect as real.
fail to reject, don't ship on this alone.
The hardest part isn't the test -- it's when you're allowed to look at it.
Checking this p-value every day while the experiment is still running inflates the false-positive rate far past 5%.
Real platforms fix the sample size upfront and check once, or use a sequential test built for continuous peeking.
